chapter: Opinions on pop music, jazz education and the business
title: Rock and roll as a fusion of folk music, and its commercialism
summary: Wilson calls today's pop garbage but sees it as a blend of blues, country and hillbilly that businessmen exploit.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Incidentally, this music that -- the pop music of today, which I call garbage, is rock and roll music, and in its best light, it is a manifestation of the fusion of the cultures. You got some of the old blues, and rock and roll or rhythm and blues and Negro culture mixed with the cowboy music and the hillbilly Turkey in the Straw music of the whites in the South, in the old days of segregation -- and this rock music is bringing all that folk music together (and some of it is smoking and stinking to high heaven. But when it gets in the hands of the business- men who drain every nickle out of it, then, they're not concerned with the folk quality of it, the artists, it's just that they can sell records, that's all they care about, they'll bring a dog in and let him bark a few notes and sell it!
But in its best sense, sociologically, this pop music of the day is a fusion of all of that man in the street music of 50 years ago -- don't you think?

This is a period of disorganization, right through here -- everything is coming together. Nothing is clear, and yet, the only thing is true in the rest of the world that is considered American -- is jazz.
And it's amazing how we are so well received as jazz musicians because of this creativity of this particular form.
